issue-23588.title: New Vite SVG logo renders incorrectly in WebKit
issue-23588.bodyHTML:
Describe the bug

The official Vite light and dark SVG logos can render inconsistently in WebKit when displayed at small icon sizes.

Affected official assets:

  • https://vite.dev/vite-light.svg
  • https://vite.dev/vite-dark.svg

These assets were introduced by #21339.

In WebKit 27 on macOS 27, rendering either SVG at approximately 24px height can produce:

  • A soft or blurry appearance
  • Color bleeding around the lightning mark
  • Incorrect dark edges or outlines
  • Incorrect interpolation around transparent regions

Chrome 153 renders the same files correctly.

The screenshot below shows the worst-case WebKit rendering: the logo is completely incorrect. In ordinary cases, WebKit is usually not this severe, but it still appears noticeably blurrier than Chrome.

WebKit issue screenshot from the downstream VitePress report:

The official SVG files contain:

  • 15 elements
  • 15 effects
  • 1 element
  • viewBox: 0 0 87 15

These filter and mask effects appear to be rasterized differently by WebKit and Chromium.

This also affects downstream consumers. VitePress documented the same issue and applied a raster fallback in vuejs/vitepress#5466.

Reproduction

https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ChisakaKanako/07226c8cc5558efd1ea7c64cfb553236/raw/index.html

Note: htmlpreview.github.io may occasionally fail to render the HTML. The issue can also be tested directly with the official vite-light.svg and vite-dark.svg files at approximately 24px height.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the reproduction URL in WebKit 27 on macOS 27.
  2. Display the official Vite light/dark SVG logos at approximately 24px height.
  3. Compare the rendering with Chrome 153 at the same size.
  4. Observe the blur, color bleeding, and incorrect edges in WebKit.

System Info

System:
  OS: macOS 27.0 (26A428)
  CPU: Apple M4
  Memory: 16 GB
  Shell: zsh 5.9

Browsers:
  WebKit: 27.0
  Chrome: 153.0.8010.53

Used Package Manager

npm

Logs

Official Vite logo SVG structure:

  • filters: 15
  • feGaussianBlur: 15
  • masks: 1
  • viewBox: 0 0 87 15

Downstream workaround and screenshots:
vuejs/vitepress#5466

Confirmed solution:

  • Replace the SVG with pre-rendered image assets, such as PNG or WebP, for small icon usage. This avoids runtime SVG filter and mask processing and produces consistent WebKit/Chromium rendering.
  • This is the solution currently used in VitePress PR #5466.

Alternative SVG fix:

  • Flatten or remove the Gaussian Blur filters and mask from the official SVG so it can render consistently without a raster fallback.

Validations

  • Follow our Code of Conduct
  • Read the Contributing Guidelines.
  • Read the docs.
  • Check that there isn't already an issue that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate.
  • Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. For example, if it's a Vue SFC related bug, it should likely be reported to vuejs/core instead.
  • Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A open a GitHub Discussion or join our Discord Chat Server.
  • The provided reproduction is a minimal reproducible example of the bug.

timeline.bodyHTML:
A fix is up in #23591.

Fix: Replaces the filter/mask-heavy source (15 <feGaussianBlur> filters plus an alpha mask) with a single pre-rasterized PNG at 10x the viewBox resolution, embedded via <image>. This is the fallback recommended in this issue and already adopted for the same assets in vuejs/vitepress#5466. File paths, extensions, and viewBox are unchanged, so no downstream consumer needs to update anything.

Testing: Rendered and visually compared both files before/after — the wordmark and gradient glow are preserved faithfully at the target icon size.

(left is Chrome 154, right is Safari 27)

It looks fine to me. Safari looks slightly blurry, but only slightly. It doesn't look similar to the "WebKit issue screenshot from the downstream VitePress report" image you shared.

(left is Chrome 154, right is Safari 27)

It looks fine to me. Safari looks slightly blurry, but only slightly. It doesn't look similar to the "WebKit issue screenshot from the downstream VitePress report" image you shared.

Sometimes, that’s the worst rendering result, which usually happens after the window is resized. Generally, WebKit looks like this:

It’s not just a little unclear—the entire file is rendered incorrectly. I mean, both situations can trigger this issue, but for this one file, WebKit always displays rendering errors; it doesn’t handle so many SVG effects very well.

ok, I reproduced by opening https://vitepress.dev multiple times.

It seems mask="url(#SVGgudELdDz)" part is ignored. This is definitely a bug in Safari / WebKit rather than a difference of rasterization.
I'd prefer waiting for WebKit to fix this.
Sometimes we have to accept that WebKit's support is always a step behind.
This is https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=325131 or maybe https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=282530 I think?

pull-23614.title: fix(worker): align worker urls in client and server when using terser

labels.name: p2-edge-case
labels.description: Bug, but has workaround or limited in scope (priority)

pull-23614.bodyHTML:
Worker urls generated in the server build must match the filenames created in the client build. This worked with the default minifier, but did not work when explicitly using terser as the minifier for client builds. This was because the terser plugin did not read its minification options from the per-environment config.

This PR updates the terser plugin to read from the per-environment config rather than the top-level config.

Review with whitespace disabled - most of the change is reformatting of the test case.

See #21871 for prior art that fixed a regression in this behaviour when using the default minifier.

I found this bug in v7.3.5, but I'm not expecting a backport. (for now I'm applying this change as a patch-package while I work through the Vite 8 update).

AI Disclosure: I used Claude to identify this problem, and author the fix and test case. Code has been reviewed by me, and the commit message / PR description is human authored.
